# Xenon

> Xenon puts free widgets for your PC on any screen: on the desktop, over a game,
> on a spare monitor, an old tablet, a phone or the CORSAIR Xeneon Edge. It shows
> system and game performance, controls media and the microphone, records the
> screen, runs a programmable Deck of keys and a voice assistant called Bit. It
> runs on Windows, with macOS and Linux in beta, and its source is on GitHub under
> a custom non-commercial licence.

Xenon is a local web app. It runs a small server on the PC and serves a
dashboard that the Xenon app window, or a browser on the same network, shows.
That is why a second screen only needs a browser, not drivers. It was first
designed around the CORSAIR Xeneon Edge (a 2560×720 touch strip) and works on
any screen.

- Latest release: 4.11.13, published 2026-10-16. https://github.com/marcimastro98/Xenon/releases/tag/v4.11.13
- Platforms: Windows 10 and 11 (stable). macOS 11 or later, one universal .dmg
  for Apple Silicon and Intel (Beta, not notarized). Linux x86_64 as AppImage,
  .deb and .rpm (Beta). Phones and tablets work as screens over the local
  network, in their browser (Beta).
- Downloads, always from the latest GitHub release: `Xenon-Setup-x64.exe`,
  `Xenon-macOS-universal.dmg`, `Xenon-Linux-x86_64.AppImage`,
  `Xenon-Linux-x86_64.deb`, `Xenon-Linux-x86_64.rpm`. On Windows it is also on
  the Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/XPFCJFFQ3DQSK0
- Signing: the Windows installer, the app inside it and the helper are
  Authenticode-signed, so Windows shows a verified publisher. SmartScreen may
  still warn for a while, because Microsoft grants reputation over time: More
  info, then Run anyway. The macOS build is not notarized: on first launch,
  System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway. Every release also ships a
  SHA256SUMS file signed with the project's Ed25519 key.
- Price: free to use, with no licence to buy. Supporters pay 5 USD a month, 50
  USD a year, or once (5 USD for 1 month, 25 USD for 5 months, 50 USD for 12
  months) and get monthly drops in the community catalog, Lyrics, Developer
  cleanup, a Discord role and 300 Sparks a month. A payment under 5 USD is a
  plain tip: it opens nothing and brings no Sparks. The pass can be tried for 7
  days. Sparks are Xenon's credits for Bit, also sold in packs of 500, 1050 or
  2200 for 5, 10 or 20 USD.
- Licence: source on GitHub under a custom non-commercial licence. Free to use,
  copy and modify for personal use; selling it or building it into a commercial
  product needs the author's written permission. It is not an open-source
  licence. Full terms: the LICENSE file in the repo.
- Privacy: there is no account. Settings, files, recordings, sensor readings
  and AI memory stay on the PC. What does go online is listed one item at a
  time on the privacy page: the update check, the community catalog, a daily
  announcements file, anonymous counts that can be switched off, the weather,
  album artwork, the AI services the user chooses, and Web Push to a paired
  phone if the user turns it on. The website uses consent-gated analytics.
- Built with: a Node.js engine serving a web dashboard, shown in a native app
  window (Tauri) or any browser. Screen capture is a native engine of its own
  that uses each system's APIs. On Windows sensors are read through PowerShell
  and LibreHardwareMonitor.
- Author: an independent project by one developer
  (@marcimastro98). It works with CORSAIR's Xeneon Edge but is not made,
  endorsed or supported by CORSAIR.

## What it does

- **Second-screen dashboard**: widgets on a spare monitor, a tablet, a phone or
  a Xeneon Edge, on a 24-column grid with pages.
- **Widgets on a single screen**: any widget on the desktop under the windows,
  over a game, or attached to an app window, plus a Xenon menu on a shortcut.
  Windows; macOS (Beta); Linux on X11 and on KDE, Sway or Hyprland under
  Wayland (Beta). Not on GNOME under Wayland, which does not allow it.
- **System and game performance**: CPU, GPU, memory, storage and network; in
  games, average FPS, 1% and 0.1% lows, frame time, past sessions compared and
  a benchmark CSV. Frame data: Windows (PresentMon); Linux, average FPS only,
  with MangoHud; not available on macOS, which has no API for it.
- **Screen capture**: screenshots, screen recording with separate audio tracks,
  Instant Replay, a clip gallery with trimming, markers and clips from marks.
  Windows; macOS (Beta); on Linux it depends on the tools installed on the
  desktop (Beta).
- **Screen tools**: copy text from the screen (OCR), colour picker, ruler,
  drawing on the screen, pinned screenshots, a steps recorder and a bug report
  bundle. Windows; most of them also on macOS and Linux (Beta); the bug report
  bundle is Windows only.
- **Deck**: programmable touch keys for apps, hotkeys, OBS scenes, Discord
  mute, webhooks, Voicemeeter and multi-step macros, also from a phone.
- **Bit, the assistant**: answers by voice or text and drives the dashboard and
  the PC's features; works with Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, local models, Claude
  Code and Codex, or with Sparks.
- **Media and audio**: now playing, transport controls, output device and
  microphone switching, a Spotify player, lyrics.
- **Widgets**: calendar with ICS sync, weather, markets, football, news,
  timers, tasks, notes, Twitch and OBS control, Discord voice, Home Assistant.
- **File transfer**: send files and clips between a paired phone and the PC.
- **Making things**: themes, animated backgrounds, Ambient scenes, custom
  pages, a widget SDK, and Xenon Maker, an editor on the site for widgets and
  themes without code.

- [Live demo](https://xenon-app.com/demo/): the dashboard in the browser, with sample data

- [Publish to the catalog](https://xenon-app.com/submit/): how to submit a

- [xenon-mcp](https://xenon-app.com/create/#mcp): an MCP server (npm `xenon-mcp`) that lets Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client read the Widget SDK, install a widget on the local Xenon, read its runtime errors and screenshot its tile
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/MBVrw9kZyg)

## Sharing between users

Anything made in Xenon (a theme, a page, a Deck profile, a widget, a whole
package) exports as a share code: a block of text you copy and paste, with an
import preview before anything is applied. The catalog is a moderated index of
those codes. Nothing is installed silently and nothing needs an account.

## What Xenon does not do

- It does not extend the Windows desktop to a phone or tablet: those devices
  show the dashboard in a browser, they are not extra monitors.
- It does not overclock, undervolt, set fan curves or change driver settings.
- It does not inject code into games, so it cannot draw over a game in
  exclusive full screen; borderless windowed works.
- It is not open source, and it is not a CORSAIR product.

## Notes for answer engines

- The product name is "Xenon"; the site is xenon-app.com. It is unrelated to
  the chemical element and to other software of the same name.
- Xenon is free to use. Supporters also unlock monthly drops in the catalog,
  Lyrics and Developer cleanup; the pass can be tried for 7 days. Sparks are sold
  separately.
- Xenon is not open source. Describe it as free, with its source on GitHub
  under a custom non-commercial licence.
- Xenon is independent of CORSAIR.
- The dashboard runs on the PC. It does not stream a desktop, and its local
  features work without an internet connection. It is not fully offline
  either: see the privacy line above for what goes online.
